opportunity.title: OJJDP FY 2026 Strategies to Support Children Exposed to Violence
opportunity.funder: Office of Juvenile Justice Delinquency Prevention
opportunity.description: This is a notice of funding opportunity (NOFO) for the OJJDP FY 2026 Strategies to Support Children Exposed to Violence. This opportunity will support the implementation of violent crime reduction strategies focused on violent juvenile offenders and improving communities' ability to help children exposed to violence in their homes, schools, and communities. Through this program the incidence and impact of violence will be reduced by strengthening local efforts to address victimization of children exposed to violence and mitigate the risk of adverse long-term effects and negative outcomes associated with children's exposure to violence.

opportunity.title: Infant-Toddler Court Program–State Awards
opportunity.description: The Infant-Toddler Court Program (ITCP) State Awards allow states and communities to support and expand use of enhanced child welfare practices in communities across the country that bring together courts, social services, and families to improve the safety, healthy development, and nurturing relationships of families with young children involved with child welfare. The ITCP State Awards support implementation of the evidence-based ITC approach in targeted communities. Awardees ensure successful implementation and expansion by spreading lessons learned to local teams in the state, tracking program outcomes, and training local ITC teams.

opportunity.title: Victims of Crime Act (VOCA) Victim Assistance subgrants
opportunity.funder: Utah Office for Victims of Crime
opportunity.description: In Utah, VOCA funding supports organizations that provide direct services to victims of crime, including counseling or referrals to counseling services, crisis and emotional support, advocacy, and help applying for victim compensation. Crime types served include domestic or family violence and child abuse or neglect.

criteria.text: State and local government agencies, private nonprofit organizations, and Native American Tribes may apply. Programs must provide direct services to victims of crime and offer the same services to victims of federal crimes as they do to all other victims.

A history of providing effective, cost-efficient services to victims of crime; direct services at no cost; help applying for crime victim compensation; required matching funds and financial support from non-federal sources; accurate program and financial records.
Applicants should demonstrate community support and collaboration with other agencies serving crime victims.
